scope: M2 private worker lease coordination, not an indexing service or hosted deployment

baseline.inspection: Migration 004 absent by source-object lookup (exit 128). Queued jobs existed but no claim/renew/settle protocol. No old worker replay or benchmark was possible.

observed: Concurrent workers claim distinct jobs and tokens.
A locked oldest job is skipped while the next queued job is claimed.
Expired work is reclaimed with a fresh token and incremented attempt count.
Expired/old tokens cannot renew or settle; duplicate completion returns false.
Heartbeat preserves or extends the existing expiration.
Retry delay blocks early claiming; third retry failure becomes RETRY_EXHAUSTED.
Expired final attempt is retired with a null lease instead of reclaimed.
Old transaction time does not revive an expired lease.
Claim rollback consumes no attempt; caller context is restored.
Completed processing can have failed evaluation quality.

checks.result: 49 passed, zero failures/skips; PostgreSQL 17.11; non-superuser migrations; restricted runtime logins; owned container removed.

developmentFindings.resolution: Corrected synthetic fixture timestamps while preserving the existing database constraint; all checks pass.

limits: Protocol is for trusted service SQL callers; supplied tenant/project scope is not authentication.
Application role retains direct table permissions; cooperating workers must use lease functions.
At-least-once processing and bounded polling; no exactly-once side-effect or throughput claim.
Indexing, process scheduling, account/key lifecycle and operations remain open. M2 is incomplete.
No portable API/dependency/schema change and no package release or hosted deployment.
No independent security audit claimed. Exact-head CI/review evidence belongs to the PR.
